definitions.explanation: The physical body of a person or animal. Used when talking about health, physical conditions, or body-related topics.
Often used idiomatically to refer to one's health or physical well-being, as in {体|からだ}に{気|き}をつける (take care of your health).

examples.japanese: {体|からだ}が{大|おお}きいですね。
examples.english: You have a big body, don't you?

examples.japanese: {体|からだ}に{気|き}をつけてください。
examples.english: Please take care of yourself (your health).
examples.notes: A common phrase used when parting or showing concern

examples.japanese: {体|からだ}は{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}ですか。
examples.english: Is your body okay? (Are you feeling alright?)

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{体|からだ}を{動|うご}かすことが{大切|たいせつ}です。
examples.english: It's important to move your body every day.

examples.japanese: {体|からだ}が{疲|つか}れている{時|とき}は、{早|はや}く{寝|ね}た{方|ほう}がいい。
examples.english: When your body is tired, it's better to go to bed early.

examples.japanese: {体|からだ}を{温|あたた}めてください。
{体|からだ}を{鍛|きた}えています。
{体|からだ}の{調子|ちょうし}はどうですか。
{体|からだ}を{壊|こわ}さないようにね。

notes:
{体|からだ} is a fundamental word referring to the physical body and by extension one's health or physical condition.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {体|からだ}に{気|き}をつける: to take care of one's health
- {体|からだ}を{動|うご}かす: to move one's body, to exercise
- {体|からだ}を{壊|こわ}す: to ruin one's health
- {体|からだ}の{調子|ちょうし}: one's physical condition

KANJI READING:
The kanji {体|からだ} is also read as たい in compounds:
- {体育|たいいく}: physical education
- {体重|たいじゅう}: body weight
- {体温|たいおん}: body temperature

RELATED:
- {身体|しんたい}: body (more formal/literary)
- {肉体|にくたい}: physical body (emphasizes flesh)
